points.v: 15 listed/large chains added ~19,000 beds in FY23-26 to 70,000+ and plan +54% to ~108,000 by FY30E; ~63% of planned beds are brownfield; ARPOB growth seen at 4-5% a year.
Government beds of only ~0.79 per 1,000 people; private care 8-15x costlier (Parliamentary committee). Apollo: India still needs 2.4 mn high-quality beds.

Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health (176th report, 7-Aug-2026): benchmark metro room rents to three-star hotels, end room-linked procedure pricing, standard packages, a hospital-price regulator. Recommendations only.
Insurance is the fastest-growing payer: 46% of Apollo's in-patient revenue in Q1FY27 (45% in FY26), growing 25% vs 16% for self-pay; insurers re-negotiate tariffs every two years.

Organised pharmacy chains are a small share of India's retail pharmacy market; Apollo (~7,440 stores) and MedPlus are the largest chains; e-pharmacy and quick-commerce players compete on delivery speed.

moat.v: 40-year brand; 150 countries send patients; transplant, oncology (proton) and cardiac programmes; Chennai children's hospital in Newsweek's list.
Largest network (~10,000 census beds); dense in Chennai (11 hospitals), Hyderabad (8), Bengaluru (10) and Kolkata; weaker in Mumbai (58% occupancy in the West) and the North.
ARPP +8% in Q1FY27 (price +4%), but 46% of revenue now comes from insurers who negotiate, and a Parliamentary panel wants caps.
Referral funnel and 49 mn app users; but the digital arm burned ~Rs2,000 cr of operating cost in FY23-26 and is only now breaking even.
Hospital ROCE 25-28% on capital excl. CWIP (company); new greenfields at ~Rs2.4 cr a census bed will dilute it for years.

critiques: The street applies 26-30x to 100% of hospital EBITDA and deducts nothing for minorities in the hospital subsidiaries (Assam, Lucknow, Ahmedabad, Imperial, Indore and others: Rs57 cr of profit in FY26, 3.4% of hospital profit). We deduct 3.4% of the hospitals' equity value plus small AHLL step-down minorities (~Rs3,830 cr, ~Rs267 a share); HealthCo minorities are excluded because NewCo is valued at Apollo's 59.6%.

NewCo is a distribution business (8.8% margin before digital costs at HealthCo, 3.2% at Keimed); valuing 'offline pharmacy' at 25x EBITDA treats it like a retailer. The Advent round (Rs2,475 cr for 12.1% in 2024) valued the combined platform at ~Rs20,000 cr of equity.

Keimed is promoter-linked, so the 25.3% of NewCo it brings in is a related-party transfer of value; the swap ratio was set by the board and approved by shareholders, but minority investors had little to compare it with.
Growth after FY28 depends on Rs7,400 cr of FY30-31 greenfields in Mumbai, Delhi, Varanasi, Ranchi and Chennai OMR; Apollo's record outside the South (West occupancy 58%) is weaker.
Pricing scrutiny: room-rent benchmarks or package caps would hit metro tertiary hospitals hardest; management argues 70% of patients pay under Rs2 lakh.
Bulls: occupancy back at 70% (established 72%), established margin ~26%, digital losses nearly gone, and the NewCo listing will crystallise value.
gaps: Keimed's standalone FY26 revenue, EBITDA and net debt are not disclosed (only Q1FY27: revenue Rs4,115 cr, EBITDA Rs134 cr); our Sep-28E Keimed EBITDA (~Rs705 cr) and zero net debt are GAM estimates.
Post-Ind AS EBITDA of the Cradle/Fertility businesses leaving AHLL is not disclosed (IGAAP Rs45 cr); continuing AHLL EBITDA is estimated.
Tax on the Cloudnine gain and the exact cash received are not disclosed; we use the ~Rs750 cr cash the company mentioned.

Minority profit by subsidiary for Q1FY27 is not disclosed: the total jumped to Rs29.7 cr (Rs8.2 cr a year earlier) and is unexplained. Segment PATs suggest at most ~Rs4 cr sits in HealthCo (PBT Rs140 cr, reported PAT Rs101 cr). We value minorities on the FY26 entity split (hospitals 3.4% of hospital profit, ~Rs86 cr Sep-28E) rather than annualising Q1; if hospital minorities really run at ~Rs25 cr a quarter, the deduction would be ~Rs1,750 cr (~Rs120 a share) larger.
